counterfactual_missing_items: No signs of intestinal perforation or obstruction on CT
No imaging evidence of appendiceal inflammation
Absolute neutrophil count not low (neutrophil percentage 85.4%)
decisive_items: Edematous thickening of the intestinal wall in the ascending colon with peripheral exudative changes.
Ascites culture yielded growth of Escherichia coli.
response.rationale: C1 and R2 share the same decisive raw spans: CT shows ascending colon wall thickening with exudative changes, and ascites culture grows E. coli, directly supporting infectious colitis. C1 adds anatomical (ascending colon) and etiological (E. coli) specificity, making it more complete. R8 has only non-specific abdominal pain/tenderness without imaging or culture support. R6 has elevated CRP/PCT but these are non-specific and not paired with a clear source. R7 relies on leukocytopenia but lacks neutropenia (ANC not low). R1, R3, R4 have no raw support spans. Thus C1 is champion, R2 runner-up.

rejected.why: No raw support spans; CT findings are non-literal and not specific for diverticulitis.
No raw support spans; symptoms and imaging are non-specific and do not confirm peritonitis as primary diagnosis.
No raw support spans; imaging shows ascending colon, not cecum-specific typhlitis.
Raw spans show abdominal pain and mild CRP/PCT elevation, but these are non-specific and lack a confirmed infection source; sepsis is too broad.
Raw spans show leukocytopenia and low absolute lymphocytes, but neutrophil percentage is high (85.4%), so neutropenia is absent; no imaging support.
Raw spans show right-sided abdominal pain and rebound tenderness, but CT shows ascending colon pathology, not appendiceal; no imaging or lab support for appendicitis.
